text.p: Brazil's public sector operational deficit in the 12 months to April was equivalent to 3.44 percent of gross domestic product, the Central Bank said Thursday.
Of the 3.44 percent deficit, the federal government accounted for 1.64 percent, states and municipalities 1.56 percent and state companies 0.24 percent, the Central Bank said in a statement.
In the primary account, which unlike the operational figures does not include debt costs, the deficit was 0.06 percent of GDP, the statement said.
In the 12 months to April 1996, Brazil posted an operational deficit of 5.47 percent of GDP and a primary deficit of 0.46 percent of GDP.

The statement also said Brazil's monetary base in April contracted 0.9 percent, according to daily averages. The bank did not provide data on the monetary base's performance over the previous 12 months.
Brazil's net public sector debt in April stood at 282.754 billion reais, or 34.5 percent of GDP, the Central Bank said.
